definition: Using a language model to score or compare outputs, which is how most reasoning work is evaluated once the answer is not a checkable string. Thirteen sources use or examine it, and the examinations are damning in a specific way: the failures are systematic rather than noisy. Judge preference scores do not correlate with concrete measures of safety, world knowledge or instruction following, because judges respond to style. Exact-match agreement with human labels — the field's standard validation metric — is shown insufficient across roughly 541,000 judgments and three protocols. Forcing raters to choose one answer where several are defensible biases validation badly enough to invert conclusions. Judges also carry a content-independent numeric prior, measurable by asking for random numbers and comparing against uniform, that varies by model, task and score range. Two constructive findings survive: accuracy improves monotonically with the reasoning tokens a judge is allowed, and pairwise comparison needs only to beat chance for aggregation guarantees to hold — which argues for ranking rather than scoring.

evidence.note: Replays one fixed reasoning trace through eleven KV cache compression methods and finds that the ones preserving final-answer accuracy are largely the ones destroying the reasoning that supports it — on AIME the accuracy ranking of compressors correlates with their chain-validity ranking at Spearman -0.95.
evidence.title: Does Accuracy Equal Evidence? Reasoning Faithfulness under KV Cache Compression

evidence.note: Holds one completed reasoning run fixed and varies only what a monitor is allowed to inspect — response, self-summary, full trace, internals — and finds the summary's value nearly vanishes once the monitor already has the prompt, so monitorability is a property of the display and the reader jointly rather than of the text.
evidence.title: How Much Does a Reasoning Summary Reveal? An Observability Ladder for Large Language Models

evidence.note: Compares two training-free intent classifiers built from summary statistics of prefill-time activations against trained heads on the same features, and finds the trade-off is not accuracy but where each fails — trained heads win fine-grained distinctions, statistical ones give better uncertainty on mixed prompts and survive adversarial rephrasing that collapses the trained heads to zero.
evidence.title: Training-Free versus Training-Based Intent Classification in LLMs: Accuracy, Robustness, and Failure Modes

evidence.note: Shows that supervised fine-tuning can install a triggered backdoor whose visible reasoning stays clean, correct and topically benign while the final answer is attacker-chosen — leaving CoT-only monitors at chance (AUC 0.44-0.55) and recovering detection only when the monitor is shown the answer alongside the trace (0.76-1.00).
evidence.title: Evading Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Through Model Poisoning

evidence.note: Supervises audio reasoning with per-question rubrics generated from the raw waveform, and keeps the signal alive as the policy improves by regenerating the rubrics from the model's own rollouts each step and pruning any criterion that every rollout satisfies or none does.
evidence.title: Reinforcement Learning with Evolving Rubrics as Rewards for Audio Reasoning

evidence.note: Synthesizes Cognitive Behavioral Therapy dialogues using a CoT strategy grounded in CBT guidelines plus a resistance orchestrator that steers simulated patients away from sycophantic compliance.
evidence.title: ODRA: Synthesizing Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Sessions with Structured Chain-Of-Thought and Dynamic Patient Resistance

evidence.note: Measures an LLM judge's latent number bias by asking it to emit random numbers, then rectifies its scoring token probabilities against that measured bias.
evidence.title: Mitigating Scoring Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge via Random Number Generation

evidence.note: Verifies correctness without training by comparing a reasoning trace's start-to-end hidden-state delta against two class centroids built from labelled experience.
evidence.title: Your Reasoning Model is Secretly a Reward Model - Optimization-Free Verification from Experience

evidence.note: Shows evaluator accuracy improves monotonically with reasoning tokens spent, and that buying compute at evaluation time can substitute for buying it at generation time.
evidence.title: Scaling Evaluation-Time Compute with Reasoning Models as Evaluators

evidence.note: Shows that when a rating task admits several defensible interpretations, forcing raters to pick one answer biases LLM-as-a-judge validation so badly that the selected judge can be up to 31% worse than the one chosen by asking raters for the set of all plausible ratings.
evidence.title: Validating LLM-as-a-Judge Systems under Rating Indeterminacy

evidence.note: Argues that faithfulness alone is insufficient for CoT monitoring and adds verbosity — whether the trace lists every factor needed to solve the task — combining the two into a monitorability score, then shows models can look faithful while omitting key factors.
evidence.title: Measuring Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Faithfulness and Verbosity

evidence.note: Builds a large standardized meta-benchmark and finds that LLM-judge preference scores do not correlate with concrete measures of safety, world knowledge or instruction following, because judges systematically prioritize style over factuality and safety.
evidence.title: Style Outweighs Substance: Failure Modes of LLM Judges in Alignment Benchmarking

evidence.note: Evaluates 21 LLM judges across three benchmarks and three protocols over ~541,000 judgments, and shows the field's standard validation metric — exact-match agreement — overstates chance-corrected discrimination by 34-41 points universally, while high test-retest reliability can coexist with severe position bias.
evidence.title: Reliability without Validity: A Systematic, Large-Scale Evaluation of LLM-as-a-Judge Models Across Agreement, Consistency, and Bias

evidence.note: Fits a structural causal model over the units of a single chain-of-thought trace using leave-one-out interventions and linear regression, producing a pairwise influence matrix between every pair of steps at a cost linear in the number of units.
evidence.title: Local Causal Attribution of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

evidence.note: Separates reasoning into procedural advancement and 'epistemic verbalization' — the token-level externalization of uncertainty — and shows that emitting doubt is what lets a model recover from silent divergence, that injecting a bare doubt cue recovers failed trajectories, and that 800 SFT examples suffice to install or destroy the habit.
evidence.title: Understanding Reasoning in LLMs through Strategic Information Allocation under Uncertainty

evidence.note: Trains a sparse autoencoder over whole reasoning steps rather than tokens, conditioning both encoder and decoder on the preceding trajectory so the sparse code carries only what the step adds, and shows that step correctness, logicality, length and first token are all linearly decodable from that code.
evidence.title: Step-Level Sparse Autoencoder for Reasoning Process Interpretation

evidence.note: Gives two aggregation algorithms whose failure probability provably decays to zero as inference compute grows, assuming only that the model can sometimes be right and can compare two solutions better than chance.
evidence.title: Provable Scaling Laws for the Test-Time Compute of Large Language Models

evidence.note: Shows that base models win pass@K on mathematics by producing wrong chains that land on right answers, and that scoring the chain too — CoT-Pass@K — reverses the verdict in RLVR's favour at every K.
evidence.title: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards Implicitly Incentivizes Correct Reasoning in Base LLMs

name: LLM-as-a-judge
